root.name: Vienna Game: Adams' Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. Bc4 Nxe4 4. Qh5 Nd6 5. Bb3 Nc6 6. d4

overview: In the Frankenstein-Dracula, Black grabs the e4 pawn and White hits with Qh5 and Bb3, then 6.d4 offers the centre pawn while Nc6 attacks. Both sides have chances: White gets a lead in development and pressure on e5/f7, Black must find the right defence. The usual game is tactical.

white_ideas.idea: Use the lead in development with Nxe4, d4 and Bb3 to attack
Hit the e5 pawn and f7 with Qh5 and Bb3

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn by ...Nd6 and ...Nc6 and then ...exd4
Trade queens or find a safe king

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after exd4, White pieces aimed at f7 and e5

character.notes: Sharp theoretical play, tactics from move four.

gambit.notes: White gave the e4 pawn; Black can keep it.

character.reason: Early tactics and an exposed queen.

gambit.reason: White is a pawn down for development.

structure.reason: Centre opens by d4 and exd4.

approach.reason: A named line of the Vienna.

level.reason: Sharp lines with theory to know.

plans.reason: White's queen and bishop aim at f7.
